title: HYPOTHESIS: candidate genetic routes to the four changes a powered-flying fish would need
status: HYPOTHESIS THROUGHOUT. Not a predicted genome, not a design, and not a claim that any of this is achievable.
constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data. No bird data is used anywhere: class Aves is this project's held-out clade, so bird flight-muscle and respiratory genetics are excluded by construction.

physics_spec.note: HYPOTHETICAL design study. Changes parameters only; the simulator equations and the measured polar are unchanged. No bird value anywhere.
what_physics_says_it_does_not_establish: that such a fish could develop (development is not simulated)
that fins of 4x area at the same section keep the measured polar
that any gill can deliver the O2 (physiology chain pending)

summary.honest_reading: Of the four required changes, only fin proportion has genetic routes in this literature, and even there no route reaches the required magnitude or addresses span and aspect ratio. The remaining three are where the biology is missing, which is the useful result of this exercise.

items.requirement: pectoral lifting area about 3.9 times the real fish's and span about 2.5 times, at a similar aspect ratio
items.verdict: This is the ONE item with real genetic routes, because fin proportion is the trait this project studied. But no route reaches the required magnitude: the largest measured increase in pectoral fin area from any single manipulation is +65% of wild type (hhip loss of function at 72 hours post fertilisation), and the requirement is +290%, a 3.9-fold area. Nothing in the fetched literature multiplies a fin's area by 3.9, and no manipulation was measured as a span or an aspect ratio at all, so the shape requirement has no sourced route even where the size one partly does. Combining levers is untested: the one double mutant that changes fin proportion (kcnh2a with lat4a) redistributes size between fins rather than scaling one fin up.

sources.quote: To determine the impacts of overexpression exogenous Xl-kcna5 , Tg + and Tg - fins at 72 hpa were treated for systemic heat shock at 37C for one hour. Then, at 7 days post amputation (dpa) (4 days post heat shock), fins were stained with the vital dye calcein ( Du et al., 2001 ) and segment length and regenerate length were measured. Interestingly, we observed a significant increase in segment length in Tg + HS + compared to the Tg - HS + siblings ( Fig. 2 A , C , E ). However, there was no accompanying change in overall regenerate length ( Fig 2 A , B , D ).

Interestingly, we found that segment length was only modestly longer in the Tg + HS + sof b123 fish compared with Tg - HS + sof b123 siblings ( Fig. 5 A , C , E ). Because the segment length phenotype is not fully rescued to WT levels, the impacts of Xl-Kcna5 overexpression are attenuated by less Cx43-GJIC. These findings suggest that bioelectricity induced by overexpression of Xl-Kcna5 requires wild-type levels of Cx43-GJIC in order to enhance segment length.

what_is_missing: No manipulation anywhere was measured as a change in span or in aspect ratio.
No route reaches a 3.9-fold area; the best measured single-gene increase is 1.65-fold and it is larval, not adult.
The two stage regimes (embryonic fin bud, mature adult) cannot be interpolated, so a larval area change is not an adult fin.
Pectoral fin LENGTH has no calibrated route at all (see interventions.json no_sourced_genetic_route).

items.requirement: a large aerobic pectoral flight muscle at about 16% of body mass, where the real fish has small fin muscles

bat_comparison.source: PMC10966098 (Onychonycteris paper, 10.1038/s42003-024-06032-9) citing Bullen and McKenzie 2004: flight muscle on average 9.13 % of body mass in extant bats, minimum 7.8 %

items.verdict: The literature run for this item has not finished, so no verdict is recorded. What this thread already holds is fin-muscle DEVELOPMENT genetics, not muscle-mass genetics: genes that decide whether fin muscle forms at all, not how much of it there is.

fin_muscle_chains_this_thread_has.weakest_link: gene->molecular_function: no Foxc1a target gene or binding experiment relevant to the fin was read, so the molecular step is association while the cell and process steps are much stronger; and the whole chain was read from the abstract only, so the rescue driver, the muscle cell identity and the synapse quantification were not inspected.

cell_or_tissue_effect->phenotype: there is no sourced cellular or developmental account of how a somitic muscle-stem-cell deficit produces an asymmetric pectoral girdle in the adult; the two ends of that step come from different papers a decade apart and nothing I fetched examines girdle cells in meox1 mutants.

gene->molecular_function: the ubiquitin-ligase activity and Delta binding come from the Itoh 2003 abstract only (full text not open) and were shown in neurogenesis, not in the fin. Also the canonical allele ta52b disrupts both mib1 and mib2; only m178 isolates mib1, and m178 was used for the muscle-fibre and actin readouts but not for the Pax7 counts.

process->phenotype: the step from mononucleate muscle to a small, porous pectoral girdle is correlative (n=3 adults per genotype, alizarin red morphology) and the authors offer two alternative mechanisms (mechanical unloading versus a direct role of the fusogens in osteoclast fusion) without testing either; nothing links mymk to fin or girdle osteoblasts.

gene->molecular_function: pax7a's molecular activity is supported only by expression and the words 'transcription factor' in a review, so that link is association; and the whole chain is a redundant requirement, since 'Pax7 alone is not required for appendicular myogenesis'.

what_is_missing: The fish muscle-mass and oxygen-delivery literature run is unfinished.

Every fin-muscle result this thread has is about whether muscle forms, not about its mass fraction: the pax7 quadruple mutant develops muscle-less pectoral fins, and met is necessary for the abductor.
A larger muscle is useless here unless it is aerobic rather than glycolytic, and fibre-type specification is a separate question from mass.
Nothing connects a fin-muscle mass change to a flight-capable power output; the physics requirement is a specific power, which no genetic result reports.

what_is_missing: The air-breathing literature run is unfinished.
A gas bladder used for respiration conflicts with its use for buoyancy, which is a design cost, not a gene.
Carbon dioxide excretion happens at the gills in water breathers, so an air-breathing fish still has to solve it.

how_to_read_this: A route is listed because an experiment changed the parameter, never because a gene sounds relevant.
Evidence grades are the project's five: association, necessity, sufficiency, mechanism, hypothesis.
An effect size appears only where a paper gives a number; most of this literature reports morphology in figures.
Pleiotropy is attached to every gene from the vetted map, because every lever here moves more than the fin.
Stage regimes do not interpolate: a larval fin measurement is not an adult fin.
